test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 06 Feb, 2026 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
In the given figure, AB is parallel to CD. Angle PRB = 74 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle DSQ?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/82408a99f742456b9da3389f92f43649d5199187a34d9cfb4b8066e193db9b19.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In parallel lines, corresponding angles are equal.

∠RSD = ∠PRB = 74°

Angles on a straight line (linear pair) sum to 180°.

∠DSQ = 180° − ∠RSD = 180° − 74° = 106°

**∴ The correct answer is 106°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** AB || CD, ∠PRB = 74°.

**Formula Used:** Corresponding angle property and Linear pair property.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c5d170cf11426376089c7c64304fa8496dc2c02e191a34bb41d4d62f2c374162.png] 

⇒ Since AB || CD and PQ is the transversal, ∠PRB and ∠RSD are corresponding angles.

⇒ ∠RSD = ∠PRB = 74°

⇒ Now, S lies on the transversal line PQ, making ∠RSD and ∠DSQ a linear pair.

⇒ ∠RSD + ∠DSQ = 180°

⇒ 74° + ∠DSQ = 180°

⇒ ∠DSQ = 180° − 74°

⇒ ∠DSQ = 106°

**∴ The correct answer is 106°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Corresponding Angles

Angles in the same relative position at each intersection where a straight line crosses two others. If the two lines are parallel, corresponding angles are equal.

Linear Pair

A pair of adjacent angles formed by intersecting lines. The sum of the angles in a linear pair is always 180°.

Alternate Interior Angles

Angles between the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal. They are always equal (∠ARS = ∠RSD).

Co-Interior Angles

Angles on the same side of the transversal between the two parallel lines. Their sum is always 180° (∠BRS + ∠RSD = 180°).
